name: std__Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance
signature: void std__Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance(RbTreeNode* header, int insert_left, RbTreeNode* x, RbTreeNode* p)
summary: libstdc++ red-black tree insertion: links the new node x below p, sets its colour/flag byte, calls the rebalance helper, then repairs the header's leftmost/rightmost child pointers. This is the insertion primitive behind every std::map/std::set in the game.
evidence: Exact structural match to libstdc++ __rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance: colour byte at node+0x10, parent +0x4, left +0x8, right +0xC (verified in asm 0x10EEA0-0x10EF60); calls 0x115290 (identified as _Rb_tree_rebalance) at 0x10EF0C; after that walks left/right spines to store leftmost/rightmost into header+8/header+0xC. 28 callers across decomp/readable (0x107F84, 0x107FC0, 0x1E88E4, 0x2ACAA4, 0x336BE4, ...) are all map/set insert sites returning iterator pairs.

name: maybe_Container_ResetObject
summary: Clears the state words at +0x38..+0x74 of an 0x8C-byte object, zeroes the whole object with memset, then sets the two flag bytes at +0x84/+0x85 and the invalid index -1 at +0x88, returning the object. Looks like a constructor/reset helper for a fixed-size table or queue object; no call site was found, so it is probably reached through a vtable or initialiser table.
evidence: asm 0x10F31C-0x10F39C: eleven str r5,[r0,#0x38..#0x6c], bl 0x116AE0 with r1=0x84 twice (0x116AE0 is memset, confirmed by its 0x20-byte store loop at 0x116AE0), strb r5,[r4,#0x84], strb r5,[r4,#0x85], mvn r0,#0; str r0,[r4,#0x88]; returns r4. No func_0010F31C callers in decomp/readable, so role is inferred from shape only.

name: Mem_AllocAligned
signature: void* Mem_AllocAligned(u32 size, MemHeap* heap, u32 alignment)
summary: Allocates size bytes with the given alignment from an engine heap: asks heap->vtable->alloc for (size+alignment+10) rounded down to 4 bytes, aligns the result with an unsigned division by alignment, and stores the heap pointer plus the untouched raw pointer in the two words before the returned block so it can be freed.
evidence: asm 0x10F6EC: ldr r0,[r5] (heap vtable), ldr r3,[r0], blx r3 with r0=heap, r1=(size+align+10)&~3, r2=4; then bl 0x11CFAC (unsigned divide helper: power-of-two subtraction loop) with r0=raw+align+7, r1=align; mul r1,r0,align; stm r0-8,{r5,r6} stores heap and raw pointer. 63 callers, e.g. 0x104A38 func_0010F6EC(0x12c00,arg3,0x10) and 0x10EAB0.

name: Container_InitList
summary: Creates the sentinel node of an intrusive doubly-linked list (0x28-byte node from 0x115F74), points the node's prev/next at itself, zeroes the list count and stores the list in the global at 0x007AED40. Returns 0 on success and -1 when the node allocation fails.
evidence: Only caller is 0x109FB0 (the GPU/device initialiser) which passes base+0x868. asm: str r0,[global 0x7AED40]; bl 0x115F74 (allocates and zeroes 0x28 bytes); str r1,[r0,#0x20]/[r0,#0x24]=0; strd r0,r1,[r2] and strd r0,r1,[r2,#8] makes node->prev=node->next=node; returns 0/-1.

name: Gfx_InitPipelineState
summary: Initialises the fixed-function GPU state block at renderer_base+0x30EC: 16 four-word attribute records (float bit patterns 0x1503/0x1406/0x8006 converted to PICA200's 24-bit float format), 16 vertex-attribute strides, default depth/blend registers (0x1E00, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFF) and a 0x40-byte zeroed table at +0x828.
evidence: Sole caller 0x109FB0 at 0x10A070 with r0 = allocation+0x30EC (asm 0x10A048-0x10A06C computes r1). Body fills the 0x298..0x3A0 arrays in pairs of floats and converts IEEE-754 to 24-bit float (mantissa>>7, exponent-0x40), a PICA200-specific format; default PICA200 register values 0x1e00/0xffffffff/0xffffff appear at +0x608/+0x60c/+0x67c; tail bl 0x111384 is memset.

name: Gfx_InitCommandLists
summary: Initialises the two renderer command-list objects (0x78-byte and 0x1CC-byte variants created by 0x116430/0x116368) and rebinds them into the global at 0x007AF07A-style context slot; old objects are torn down through 0x115DCC/0x1164C8 before being replaced.
evidence: Only caller 0x109FB0 at 0x10A0C0 passes base+0x2840. asm stores arg in 0x7AFxxx, calls 0x116430(0), 0x116368(0), stores them into the context, then loops 6 times over 0x44-byte records calling 0x115DCC + 0x1164C8(iVar5->f_2c, rec+0x34) to release the previous lists; a free callback is invoked for each old block.

name: Gfx_InitRenderQueue
summary: Stores the queue object in a global and creates its backing store with 0x1165B0 (a 0x348-byte array of 16 slots x 0x18 bytes plus 16 texture references). Returns 0 on success and -1 after calling the deallocation callback when the store cannot be created.
evidence: Only caller 0x109FB0 at 0x10A098 passes base+0x878. Body: str arg in 0x7Axxxx, bl 0x1165B0, str result at [*g+0x800]; on failure invokes function pointer *g_00110694(0x10000,0x100,0) and clears the global. 0x1165B0 builds 16 records of 0x18 bytes plus 16 texture entries (see its body).

name: Gfx_InitSubsystems
summary: Stores the subsystem set in a global and runs the four subordinate initialisers attached at +4, +8 and +0xC (0x115F4C, 0x115E5C, 0x11C5E8, 0x115E70). Always returns 0.
evidence: Only caller 0x109FB0. asm 0x11069C-0x1106D0: str r0,[0x7AE8E8]; bl 0x115F4C; bl 0x115E5C(*(g)+4); bl 0x11C5E8(*(g)+8); bl 0x115E70(*(g)+0xC); mov r0,#0. The four calls are pure initialisers (none returns a checked value), matching an SDK 'initialise sub-managers' step.

name: Gfx_RegisterResource
signature: void Gfx_RegisterResource(u32 key, GfxResource* res, u32 unused)
summary: Inserts a 0x44-byte resource record into a 32-bucket hash table (buckets at 0x007E7780, next pointer at +0x40), keeping each bucket sorted by key, and updates the current-range globals at 0x007E8320/0x007E8324 from the record's base/size fields.
evidence: Only caller 0x109FB0 (with key 1). asm: key&0x1f selects bucket at 0x7E7780+4*k; walks node->+0x40 chain comparing *node; allocates a 0x44-byte node through the callback at *0x7E8334; node[0]=key; node[0xb]=0x300; then updates the range/limit globals 0x00110850/0x00110854 as node[3]+base and node[2]+base. 0x110858 is the matching removal routine, which confirms it is a resource registry.

name: Gfx_UnregisterResources
summary: Removes the given keys from the 32-bucket resource table, dropping the cached 'current resource' pointers, calling the resource destructor callback and the block-free callback for each match, and lowering the cached minimum address.
evidence: Companion of 0x1106F0 (same bucket array 0x7E7780, next at +0x40). Loops over keys, unlinks the node, clears the cached pointers 0x00110990/0x00110994, calls the destructor callback at 0x7E8334+4 with (0x10000,0x100,0,node), lowers the cached minimum 0x7E8338+8, and frees the node with (0x10000,0x100,0,node).

name: maybe_Gfx_GetLcdWidth
summary: Returns the cached LCD width: for the 0x30000 GSP command it asks 0x11981C and returns the global width, otherwise 0. The condition register (ZR) guard shows this is the tail of a Thumb/dual-entry helper.
evidence: Body: if (ZR) { func_0011981C(); return g_001109D4; } if (arg1 == 0x30000) { func_0011981C(0x30000); result = g_001109D0; }. Globals 0x1109D0/0x1109D4 are the width values filled by the GSP display-info query; 0x1109DC is the height twin.

name: maybe_Gfx_GetLcdHeight
summary: Returns the cached LCD height (global 0x110A1C) or the default 0x1F000000 constant when the GSP display-info query fails; the 0x30000 command selects the same display as 0x1109A0.
evidence: Mirror image of 0x1109A0: calls 0x11981C(0x30000), returns g_00110A1C when it succeeds and g_00110A20 (=0x1F000000, a fixed 31.0 value) on failure; the ZR branch returns g_00110A24 or 0x1F000000. Pairs with the width getter used by the framebuffer setup.

name: Gfx_PushPipelineCommand
summary: Appends one 0x1C-byte command to the renderer's pending command array (record type 1), fills in the destination address/size from the current cursor, submits it through 0x116104 and advances the queue counters; if this was the last pending command it starts a new frame via 0x116104.
evidence: Readable 0x110A28: f_18 + f_20*0x1c record, *record=1, +4 = f4+f14, +8 = fc-f14, optional 0x1160AC, updates f_20, then func_001197FC/0x116104/0x11980C. Sole caller 0x109FB0 at 0x10A...; record layout and type dispatch (types 0..4) are in 0x116104, confirming this writes one command node.

name: Gfx_WaitForVBlank
summary: Blocks until the GSP frame counter changes for the requested screen: 0x400 (top) and 0x402 (both/top+bottom) poll the per-screen counters at context+0x154/0x158 and release the CPU with 0x113700; other values wait for 0x119388.
evidence: Readable: if (arg1 != 0x402) { iVar4 = ctx + (arg1 != 0x400)*4; do { func_00113700(); iVar5 = iVar4->f_154; } while (iVar3 == iVar5); ... } else polls both f_154 and f_158. f_154/f_158 are the counters incremented by the VBlank handlers 0x110D34/0x110D78, which the GPU driver installs for displays 0x400/0x402.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitFrameCommand
signature: void Gfx_SubmitFrameCommand(u32 opcode, u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f)
summary: Thunk that forwards the frame's seven parameters to 0x113714, which appends a command record to the renderer's command ring (see 0x113714). Called once per frame by the display update at 0x10AD60.
evidence: Only caller 0x10AD60; body is literally 'bl 0x113714; bx lr', so Ghidra shows no arguments. 0x113714 takes 7 register arguments and writes a 0x1c-byte record plus an atomic 0x100 flag; the caller passes a 7-word GPU command descriptor.

name: Gfx_OnVBlankTop
summary: Top-screen VBlank interrupt handler: invokes the registered callback with display id 0x400 and advances the frame counter at context+0x154 modulo 0x7FFFFFFF.
evidence: Body: if (ctx->f_15c) ctx->f_15c(0x400); iVar2 = ctx->f_154 + 1; ctx->f_154 = iVar2 + ((iVar2 * 0x40000001) >> 61) * -0x7FFFFFFF (the compiler's signed-modulo-by-0x7FFFFFFF idiom). 0x110BC0 waits on exactly this counter for display 0x400, and 0x110D78 is its 0x402 twin.

name: Gfx_OnVBlankBottom
summary: Bottom/sub-screen VBlank interrupt handler: invokes the registered callback with the 0x402 display id (global 0x110DBC) and advances the second frame counter at context+0x158 modulo 0x7FFFFFFF.
evidence: Identical to 0x110D34 except it uses ctx->f_160 / ctx->f_158 and passes g_00110DBC (the 0x402 display id) to the callback; 0x110BC0 polls both counters when waiting for 0x402.

name: Gfx_InitCommandRing
signature: void Gfx_InitCommandRing(GfxCommandRing* ring, u32 capacity, u32 arg3)
summary: Initialises a lock-protected command ring: stores capacity and the caller tag, resets the two atomic counters and read/write cursors under ldrex/strex, sets both 'ready' halfwords from the current system tick, and obtains the initial tick from 0x111288.
evidence: Readable: *arg1=arg2; arg1[6]=arg3; arg1[9]/[10]/[1..4]=0 with hasExclusiveAccess loops (ldrex/strex spinlocks); *(short*)(arg1+10)=low16(tick); calls 0x111288(&local,0) which is the svc #0x13 wrapper and stores the 64-bit tick in arg1[5]. Sole caller 0x108C5C, part of the GSP shared-memory setup.

name: Gfx_PopCommandRing
summary: Removes one entry from the command ring: takes the lock (svc 0x24), validates the ring's result word, reads the word at the read cursor, advances it modulo capacity, decrements the pending count and wakes a waiter; returns 1 when an entry was produced and 0 when the ring is empty.
evidence: Readable: software_interrupt(0x24) (lock), if (arg1[5] < 0) error path, if (arg1[8] > 0) { *arg2 = *(u32*)(*arg1 + arg1[7]*4); func_0011CFAC(arg1[7]+1, arg1[6]) (modulo capacity); arg1[7]=remainder; --arg1[8]; if (arg1[10]>0) func_00117DC4(arg1+3,1); ... return 1; } return 0. Mirrors Gfx_InitCommandRing's layout.

name: std_strncpy
signature: char* std_strncpy(char* dst, const char* src, int n)
summary: newlib strncpy: copies at most n bytes from src to dst, using the usual word-at-a-time zero-byte test when both pointers are aligned, stops after copying the terminating NUL and zero-fills the remainder of the n-byte destination.
evidence: asm 0x111430: tst r0,#3 / tsteq r1,#3 fast path, ldr with mask 0x7EFEFEFF-style test ('uVar4 - iVar3 & ~uVar4 & iVar3 << 7'), then byte loop that breaks on NUL, then bl 0x1113EC (memset body) for the remaining count. The tail memset is the strncpy zero-pad; 0x1113EC and 0x116AE0 are the two memset variants.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd803
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmd803(u32* session, u32* out, u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e, u32 f, u32 g, u32 h, u32 i, u32 j)
summary: IPC client stub for command 0x0803 (8 normal + 4 translated parameters) to the GPU service: fills the thread-local request buffer at TPIDRURO+0x80 and returns the service result, copying back two output words. Called by the renderer at 0x504378/0x505058 and by the SDK at 0x10B524/0x10B830.
evidence: asm 0x111AA0: mrc p15,0,r4,c13,c0,3 (__aeabi_read_tp), header g_00111B3C = 0x08030204 (cmd 0x803, 8 normal / 4 translate), stores 8 words at TLS+0x84.. and r0/r1 outputs at +0x8c/0x90, svc 0x32 (SendSyncRequest). Callers 0x504378/0x505058 are engine render code (they also call 0x117B78/0x117C58 semaphores).

name: Gfx_IpcCmd861
summary: IPC client stub for command 0x0861 (1 normal + 2 translated parameters) to the GPU service; used to push a single dword (typically a GPU/interrupt selector) and return the service result.
evidence: asm: header g_00111B74 = 0x08610042 (cmd 0x861, 1 normal/2 translate), TLS +0x84 = arg2, +0x88 = 0x20, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x10B6AC, inside the same GPU init/IRQ code that calls Gfx_IpcCmd803.

name: Gfx_WaitGpuInterrupt
summary: Waits for a GPU interrupt by issuing the GPU service command 0x40000 (via 0x117B18) and converts the usual 'would block' result 0xFFFFF9 into a normal return while asserting on real errors.
evidence: Body: result = func_00117B18() (cmd 0x40000 stub); if (result < 0) { uVar3 = result >> 27; if (uVar3 != -7) func_0011ED40(result, assert_site); } The -7 (0xFFFFF9) special case is the SDK's 'try again' result; caller 0x10BA40 also calls 0x111BEC, so the pair waits on two interrupt sources.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseGpuInterrupt
summary: Issues GPU service command 0x30000 (via 0x117B48) and clears the cached interrupt counters at context+4/+8 on success; errors other than the 0x19/0xFFFFxxxx 'already clear' result are asserted.
evidence: Body: result = func_00117B48() (0x30000 stub); if (result < 0) assert unless result>>27 == 0x19 or result == g_00111C4C; else { *(g_00111C50+4)=0; *(g_00111C50+8)=0; }. Paired with 0x111BAC (0x40000) as the two halves of the GSP interrupt handshake.

name: maybe_Os_SetSyncState
summary: Atomically replaces the state word of a synchronisation object with -1 (mode 0) or -2 (mode != 0) and returns the previous state. Used to force a wake-up/failure state on a thread or event object.
evidence: Body: func_00117C40(obj+1) (lock/link), uVar3 = (arg2==0) ? 0xffffffff : 0xfffffffe; do { result=*obj; } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(obj)); *obj=uVar3. 16 callers spread over engine modules (0x102AE8, 0x103544, 0x10BB34, 0x10C8C4, 0x10D6CC, 0x11896C, 0x18F974 ...), so it is a generic OS helper; the exact meaning of -1/-2 is not recoverable.

name: Os_CreateThreadWithStack
signature: int Os_CreateThreadWithStack(u32* out_handle, OsThreadParams* params, u32 entry, u32 arg, int stack_top, u32 stack_size, u32 priority, int detached)
summary: Creates a detached or joinable OS thread: computes the aligned stack top from the caller-supplied stack region, writes the thread argument block, then calls svcCreateThread (0x1112A0) with entry/arg/stack/priority and optionally patches the stack chunk header.
evidence: Readable: uVar4 = (stack_top - *params) & ~7; if (!detached) stack_top = 0; calls params->[1](arg, uVar4) (stack guard/clear hook); writes a 0x18-byte chunk header at uVar4-0x18; then func_001112A0(&local, g_0011204C, entry, entry, size, priority) - 0x1112A0 is 'svc #8' (CreateThread), verified in asm 0x1112A0. Callers include 0x1076AC, 0x10BB34, 0x119498, 0x517884.

name: maybe_Os_CallFinalizers
summary: Runs up to eight registered finaliser callbacks (table at 0x00112380) once, then clears the 'initialised' flag at 0x0011237C+2. Used during shutdown of the SDK subsystem that owns the table.
evidence: Readable: if (*(char*)(g_0011237C+2)) { for (i=0;i<8;i++) if (g_00112380[i]) g_00112380[i](); *(u8*)(g_0011237C+2)=0; }. Table of 8 function pointers and one flag; sole caller 0x10CF50, which also calls 0x114344/0x119DF8 (shutdown path).

name: Hid_DispatchPadReport
signature: void Hid_DispatchPadReport(HidCalibration* cal, u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d)
summary: Dispatches a raw pad report to one of three calibration/decoding paths depending on the report-type byte at +0xC (0 = 0x11FBCC, 1 = 0x11A810 circle-pad, 2 = 0x11A914 touch/other), passing the two pairs of 16-bit axis values.
evidence: Body: cVar1 = *(char*)(arg1+0xC); if 0 -> func_0011FBCC(arg2,arg3,arg4,arg5,*arg1,arg1[3]); if 1 -> func_0011A810(...,arg1[1],arg1[4]); if 2 -> func_0011A914(...,arg1[2],arg1[5]). Callers 0x10C2D4 and 0x112640 are the two pad-reader paths; 0x11A810 is the 936-byte circle-pad calibration routine.

name: Hid_ReadPadState
summary: Reads one pad snapshot from the HID service (0x11ABB8) into out_state, computes the newly-pressed / newly-released masks against the previous state, applies the circle-pad calibration and returns 1 when a report was produced, 0 otherwise.
evidence: Readable: if (func_0010C51C()==0) { ...; func_0x0011ABB8(*(u32*)(*arg1+4),arg2,1,local...); if (local[0] > 0) { func_00112518(...); *arg1[2]=*arg2; uVar2=*arg2&~0x2000; arg2[1]=(uVar2^arg1[2])&~arg1[2]; arg2[2]=arg1[2]&~uVar2; ... return 1; } } The pressed/released masks in arg2[1]/arg2[2] are the classic HID button-edge computation.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd60040
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0006 with one translated parameter; returns the service result or the output word on success.
evidence: asm 0x112774: header 0x00060040 (cmd 6, 1 translate), TLS+0x84=arg1, svc 0x32, returns TLS+0x84. No callers in decomp/readable; grouped with the other GSP stubs by the shared request layout and the 0x60040 header.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd140040
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0014 with one translated parameter; returns the service result or the echoed output word.
evidence: asm 0x1127B0: header g_001127E0 = 0x00140040, TLS+0x84=arg1, svc 0x32, returns TLS+0x84 on success. No callers; same family as 0x112774.

name: maybe_Gfx_DispatchPendingCommands
summary: Tail-call wrapper around 0x1129F4, used by the frame loop at 0x107628 to drain pending GPU commands before the next present.
evidence: Body is 'bl 0x1129F4; bx lr' (20 bytes). Sole caller 0x107628; 0x1129F4 is the actual worker, so the entry is only a nameable thunk and its role is inferred from the caller's position in the render loop.

name: maybe_Svc_IpcCmdB0000
summary: IPC stub for command 0x000B0000 (no parameters) on the srv: session whose handle is stored at 0x007AF900; returns the service result and writes the 0x88 output word to *out. The neighbouring srv: initialiser at 0x1134xx references the 'srv:' name string at 0x741AD8.
evidence: asm 0x113554: header 0xB0000, TLS+0x80, svc 0x32, handle loaded from *0x7AF900 (0x11358C). The literal pool at 0x113540 holds 0x741AD8 = pointer to 'srv:' (found in rodata), belonging to the srv initialiser directly before this stub. No callers in the readable tree because it is reached through the SDK init table.

name: Gfx_WriteHwRegs
signature: void Gfx_WriteHwRegs(u32 addr, u32 value, u32 count)
summary: Writes GPU hardware registers through the GPU service: obtains the session handle from the thread-local GSP state and calls 0x1196B0, which issues command 0x00010082.
evidence: Body: uVar1 = func_0011F730() (current GSP session); func_001196B0(uVar1, arg1, arg2, arg3). 0x1196B0's header is 0x00010082 - the GSPGPU WriteHWRegs command (addr/value/count are exactly the three parameters).

name: Gfx_QueueCommand
signature: void Gfx_QueueCommand(u32 queue_id, u32 opcode, u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e)
summary: Appends a 0x1C-byte command to one of the two renderer command queues kept in thread-local storage, writes the six parameter words, issues a data-synchronisation barrier and sets the entry's valid/pending bit with an ldrex/strex.
evidence: Readable: if (arg1 < 2) { pbVar4 = *(u8**)(tls + 0x5c + arg1*4); idx = 1 - *pbVar4; pbVar4 += idx*0x1c + 4; write arg2..arg7; coproc_moveto_Data_Synchronization(0); ldrex *pbVar4 = (*pbVar4 & 0xffff0000) | idx | 0x100; }. Caller 0x110C70; the queue base at TLS+0x5c is filled by 0x1136D8's session setup.

name: Os_IsInHeapRange
summary: Returns 1 when addr lies inside either the main heap or the second (linear/VRAM) heap range, otherwise 0; used by the debug/assert path to decide whether a pointer is a real allocation.
evidence: Readable: uVar1 = func_001180F0(); iVar2 = func_001180E0(); if range1 contains arg1 -> 1; else uVar1 = func_00122CD8(); iVar2 = func_00122CC0(); if (uVar1==0 || arg1<uVar1 || iVar2+uVar1<=arg1) return 0; return 1. The two (base,size) pairs are the engine heaps; no callers because it is called from an inline assert macro.

name: Gfx_WriteHwRegsWithMask
signature: void Gfx_WriteHwRegsWithMask(u32 addr, u32 value, u32 mask, u32 count)
summary: Writes GPU hardware registers with a bit mask through the GPU service by calling 0x11979C, whose command header is 0x00020084 (GSPGPU WriteHWRegsWithMask).
evidence: Body: func_0011979C(func_0011F730(), arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4); 0x11979C issues header 0x00020084 with (addr,value,mask,count). Pairs with 0x1136D8 (plain write).

name: maybe_Gfx_InitInterrupts
summary: Clears the caller's interrupt-enabled flag, then registers GPU interrupt callbacks (0x113A40 for three sources) and enables interrupts through 0x1143C8; the ZR test shows the real entry is a Thumb/dual-mode helper.
evidence: Readable: *arg1 = 0; if (!ZR) { func_00113A40(3); func_001143C8(...); }. No callers; 0x113A40 is a 0x100+ byte routine and 0x1143C8 is the lock helper, so this is an interrupt/subsystem bring-up step rather than a leaf.

name: maybe_Svc_IpcCmd50100
summary: Submits the 32-bit value as a four-word IPC request (command 0x00050100) through 0x119A10, which forwards it to the GPU/OS service and waits for completion.
evidence: Body: auStack_8[0]=arg1; func_00119A10(7, auStack_8, 4, 0, 0, 0). 0x1196B0-family header 0x50100 (cmd 5, 4 normal params) is built by 0x119348; the '7' is the command selector. Only caller 0x10CF50 (shutdown).

name: maybe_Os_LockScheduler
summary: Takes the SDK's global scheduler/GPU lock (0x119BA8 + 0x1198CC), calls 0x11A3E8 with the argument, and releases it via 0x119E1C; asserts when 0x11A3E8 reports an error.
evidence: Body: func_00119BA8(); uVar1=func_001198CC(); iVar2=func_0011A3E8(uVar1,arg1); if (iVar2<0) func_00118924(iVar2,assert_site); func_00119E1C();. The same lock/unlock pair surrounds every GSP call (0x1198DC, 0x11A140, 0x119A10), so it serialises access to the GPU service.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd1010000
summary: IPC stub with header 0x01010000 (no parameters) to the same session as the other GPU stubs; returns the result and writes the byte at TLS+0x88 to *out.
evidence: asm 0x114584: header literal 0x1010000, TLS+0x80 = header, load handle from 0x7AF0D8, svc 0x32, if success *out = *(u8*)(TLS+0x88). The 0x7AF0D8 handle is shared by all stubs in this batch.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd3B0040
summary: IPC stub for command 0x003B with one byte parameter and one translated parameter; returns the service result or the echoed value.
evidence: asm 0x114614: header g_00114648 = 0x003B0040, TLS+0x84 = arg1, svc 0x32, return TLS+0x84. Sole caller 0x10DA64 in the input/display code.
